# Business proposal #1: Revisa

Status: **rejected by founder: Students rarely pay for apps here. I want a customer who already spends money on revision: tutoring centres.** · Mate's recommendation: **VALIDATE CAREFULLY**

> A free web planner that turns a student's exam dates and course load into a revision schedule.

## Problem
University students with six or seven courses and overlapping exam dates plan revision in notebooks or chat groups and often abandon the plan within a week. (ASSUMPTION based on the founder's own observation; not yet confirmed by interviews.)

## Target customer
Undergraduate students at the founder's university during exam season.

## Proposed solution
A browser-based planner where a student enters courses and exam dates and gets a day-by-day revision plan they can tick off.

## Founder–idea fit (heuristic 4/5)
The founder is a student in this situation, can build the web app, and can reach classmates directly. Gap: no clear payer.

## Unique value proposition
A realistic revision plan in five minutes instead of an abandoned notebook schedule.

## Business model and revenue streams
Free at launch; a paid premium tier later (price and willingness to pay untested).

- Optional premium plan for students (untested)

## Main expenses (all ASSUMPTION unless marked)
| Item | Estimate | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Domain and basic hosting | 1,200 EGP per year — ASSUMPTION | Rough assumption; prices not retrieved. |
| Campus outreach materials | 1,500 EGP one-time — ASSUMPTION | Leaflets for student areas; rough assumption. |

Estimated start-up capital: 3,000 EGP first 3 months — ASSUMPTION. Sum of assumed expenses plus a small contingency.

## Competitive alternatives
- **Google Calendar** — Free calendar some students already use for deadlines. *(named in debate; existence checked in Phase 1 research)*
- **Notion** — Free templates for study planning. *(named in debate; existence checked in Phase 1 research)*
- **Paper planners and WhatsApp groups** — The current status quo. *(named in debate; existence checked in Phase 1 research)*

## Major risks
- Students may not pay for any tier.
- Free alternatives already exist.
- Abandoning plans may be a motivation problem, not a tooling problem.

## Missing evidence
- Whether students would pay at all
- How many students abandon plans and why
- Which features would change that behaviour

## First validation experiment
**Student waitlist test** — Share a one-page landing page in three course groups and count sign-ups.
Target: **100 waitlist sign-ups within 14 days** (declared before any results). About 100 sign-ups in two weeks from three large course groups would show interest beyond friends.

## Reasons for
- Founder is the target user and can reach users today.
- Cheap and quick to build.

## Reasons against
- No identified payer.
- Many free substitutes.
- 'Monetise later' often means never.

## Recommended next action
Run the waitlist test and ask every sign-up one question about paying, before building.
